errorCodes.meaning: The request has already been claimed by another key. Carries no details, so a second scanner learns nothing about the first.
The request's claim window has passed, or the request has otherwise ended.
The document's issuer is not an Ed25519 `did:key`.
The approver's network has hit the service's claim limit. `details.retryAfter` MAY give seconds until a retry.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Origin.description: A web origin (`https://host[:port]`, no path, no trailing slash) — for `login`, the origin of the portal where the starter runs, which is the origin of the `serviceEndpoint` of the service's `SignInPortal` service in its DID document.
Origin.title: Origin

Purpose.description: What the request is for. A CLOSED list: each purpose has a fixed row in CONVENTIONS.md §3 stating what is revealed at each step, what the grant contains, what redeem returns and the window lengths. Version 0.1 defines `login` only. `stepUp` and `deviceEnrol` are reserved names; adding one is a new version of this component and of every task that references it, never an in-place edit.
Purpose.title: Purpose

RequestId.description: The service-generated handle of one request: 16 to 32 bytes from a cryptographically secure random source, written as unpadded base64url (22 to 43 characters; 16 bytes, 22 characters, is RECOMMENDED). It is also the nonce of the exchange, so the family needs no separate challenge, and it is the `_id` of the trigger link (VTI-LNK-033). Compared as a string. It confers no authority on its holder.
RequestId.title: RequestId

Response.description: Step 1 of the disclosure ladder, signed by the service's assertionMethod key: who the service is, where the request will be used and for what, and when the decision window closes. It MUST contain nothing about the starter.

decisionClosesAt.description: When the decision window, started by the claim, closes, as an RFC 3339 date-time. Prove, respond and redeem must all complete before it. At most 180 s after the claim; 120 s RECOMMENDED.

Response.title: Auth — OOB Claim — response payload (step 1)

Service.description: Who the service says it is.

did.description: The service's DID: the `recipient` of every request in the family, and the `_from` of the trigger link.

name.description: The name the service calls itself. Supplied by the service: an approver shows the name from its OWN records and flags a difference from this one (VTI-LNK-104); it never shows this value as the community's name on its own authority.

Service.title: Service

schema.description: An approver claims a pending out-of-band request, locking it to a throwaway Ed25519 key (`K_a`) generated for this one exchange. The document is the first request of a trigger-link exchange (VTI-LNK-054): issued and signed by `K_a`, addressed to the service, and carrying the request's handle both here and as the envelope's `parentThreadId`. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, parentThreadId, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

requestId.description: The handle read from the trigger link's `_id`. MUST equal the document's `parentThreadId`.

schema.title: Auth — OOB Claim — payload
